observation.visible_scene: A tight close-up of a transparent glass mug with a handle on the left, filled nearly to the brim with a dark hot beverage. A person's bare fingers grip the mug at the far left edge. A bright out-of-focus light source sits in the upper-left, casting a strong lens flare, and a greenish-blue circular flare artifact appears on the liquid surface. The background is dark, with a warm-toned surface visible at the bottom right. Wisps of steam rise from the drink throughout.
visible_changes: Steam is already rising at the start and continues to evolve: early frames show a faint puff drifting up from the center of the rim, which thickens into a vertical column around the middle of the clip, then thins and drifts leftward toward the bright light before fading.
Later in the segment new steam wisps reappear near the center/rim and again drift upward and sideways, indicating continuous, unbroken evaporation rather than a single event.
The liquid surface shows subtle shimmering and shifting micro-texture (tiny bubbles and reflections) frame to frame, but the overall fill level and rim position stay constant.

The hand, the mug body, the handle, the bright light source, and the green circular flare remain fixed in their relative positions across all frames, so the apparent motion is from the steam and surface shimmer, not from object or camera translation.
outside_clip_unknowns: What produced the heat or filled the mug, and whether the drink is coffee, tea, or another liquid, is not shown.
Whether the hand or camera moves before or after this cropped window is unknown.
The fate of the steam beyond the top edge of the frame is unseen.
uncertain_details: Any camera motion is minimal and uncertain; the stable flare and mug position suggest a near-static shot, but tiny drift cannot be ruled out.
The exact cause of the surface shimmer (steam turbulence, slight vibration, or lighting flicker) is not determinable from the frames.
The precise boundary between the green flare artifact and the liquid is optical reflection, not a physical object on the surface.
